_README: RM MODULE PLANTS TEMPLATE
This file defines HOST PLANTS: plants that exist to carry materials.
DF only stores and lists some materials properly as plant materials,
dyes above all (guide section 4.1, On DYE).
HOW TO USE THIS FILE:
1. Copy it into your mod's data/ folder.
2. Rename it to <yourmod>_plants.json.
3. Change the module block below to your own prefix, name, version.
4. Replace the plants array with your own content.
5. Hand it to RM from your listener as plants_json, the way
rm-module-template-advanced.lua hands over its files.
THE UNDERSCORE CONVENTION:
Any key starting with an underscore is documentation. RM's engine
reads only the keys it knows about, so _README and _comment are
ignored at load time. Keep them, edit them, or delete them.
PREFIXING:
You write keys. Plant key DYE_HOST under prefix MYMOD_ becomes the
plant MYMOD_DYE_HOST. Its material MY_DYE is named everywhere by
the token PLANT_MAT:MYMOD_DYE_HOST:MY_DYE, so write material keys
WITHOUT the prefix. Reactions name these materials with mat_token.
HOW A HOST IS BUILT:
RM clones a donor plant for structure, resets the donor's own
identity, writes your plant fields, then your materials. A host
that declares no materials keeps its donor's, which preflight
warns about.
VALIDATION:
RM's validator does not check this file. The plant injector guards
each plant and logs what it could not do. Run preflight, which does
check it.
FULL FIELD DOCUMENTATION:
RM_MODULE_ENGINE_README.md, section 7.2.

module._comment: Identity block. Keep it the same as your other files: RM injects plants under the module's prefix, taken from your materials or reactions file.
module.name: RM Module Template

plants._comment: REFERENCE ENTRY. Every field the schema accepts, on a plant and on one of its materials. Copy it, then delete the lines you do not need.
plants._comment_key: Required. Uppercase, no spaces: it becomes part of a raw token. The plant's ID is prefix + key.
plants._comment_name: The plant's own names. name is required by preflight.
plants.name: reference host
plants._comment_donor_plant: Optional. The ID of the plant RM clones for structure. Leave it out and RM picks one.
plants._comment_plant_flags: Optional. Plant flags by their DF names, each true or false, written after RM resets the donor. An unknown name is logged.
plants._comment_materials: The host's materials, each with the fields below. Preflight requires at least one.

materials._comment_key: Required. Uppercase, no spaces, without your prefix. The material's token is PLANT_MAT:<plant ID>:<key>.
materials._comment_name: name is required by preflight: it is what items of the material display. names overrides single states: solid, liquid, gas, powder, paste, pressed. Without names: name, molten <name>, boiling <name>, then name for the rest.
materials.name: reference dye
materials._comment_class: Optional. The flag preset: METAL, STONE, GEM, CERAMIC, GLASS, SOIL, LIQUID, DYE or RAW (guide section 4.1). A dye uses DYE.
materials._comment_color: Set it. A descriptor colour ID: the material's colour (guide section 4.3). fallback_colors are tried in order when it is not loaded. A plant material with neither loaded takes descriptor colour 7.
materials._comment_dye_color: Optional, DYE only. A descriptor colour ID to dye with, when it should not be the material's own colour. One that is not loaded is logged, and the material's own colour is used.
materials._comment_ascii: Optional. ASCII mode only: display_color colours the tile, build_color the constructions, each [foreground, background, brightness] from 0 to 7.
materials._comment_heat: Optional, every field independently optional; null keeps the donor plant material's value. Urists: 10000 is freezing, 12000 is magma (guide section 4.4).
materials._comment_strength: Optional. yield, fracture and strain_at_yield, each with IMPACT, COMPRESSIVE, TENSILE, TORSION, SHEAR and BENDING, plus max_edge and absorption, as in the materials file (guide section 4.6).
materials._comment_reaction_classes: Optional. Tags reagents can ask for (guide section 4.5).
materials._comment_graphics: Optional. Sprites for the material's own slots: bar, boulder, wood, rough, cheese, texflag. Each is a source string or a table { donor, offset } (guide section 4.7). A slot does not take the material's colour on its own; a TINT: source draws registered art in it.

plants._comment: EXAMPLE. A dye host carrying two dyes. Reactions make them with mat_token PLANT_MAT:RM_TEMPLATE_DYE_HOST:BLUE_DYE and PLANT_MAT:RM_TEMPLATE_DYE_HOST:RED_DYE.
plants.name: dye host
